answer: Each identity posts a 70-credit bond in the quartz registry and publishes a sonnet record on the meadow board: a 14-checkpoint work log. Auditors stake 20 credits and recompute every checkpoint; a clean record returns the bond, so honesty costs one 20-credit fee. Fees rise with demand: the k-th identity pays 20+3(k-1) credits, so the 1000th fake pays 3017 and 1000 fakes pay 1,518,500 in fees plus 70,000 locked. A rented-audit ring fails because anyone can recompute the checkpoints; a mismatch burns the fake bond and the auditor's stake, and reusing one sonnet record burns both bonds.
